title: Nona: Accurate Power Prediction Model Using Neural Networks
problem: Existing linear regression-based power models struggle to accurately predict power consumption of heterogeneous CPUs on mobile devices with aggressive on-device power management across diverse applications.
motivation: Accurate power prediction is critical for effective power management on mobile devices with heterogeneous processors.
method: Nona trains a lightweight neural network on performance monitoring counters (hardware measurements showing how the CPU is running), selecting only the most relevant ones through system analysis. The model uses a custom loss function (a technique that helps the network focus specifically on accurate power prediction), and was validated on a Google Pixel 6 phone.
key_novelty: Nona achieves 3.4% average error by analyzing the system to choose the right hardware measurements, then using a neural network with a loss function specifically designed for power prediction.
contributions: Lightweight neural network-based power prediction model for heterogeneous mobile CPUs
Systematic methodology for selecting relevant performance monitoring counters via system analysis
Custom loss function optimized for power prediction accuracy
3.4% average prediction error on commercial mobile device with 2.6x improvement over prior work
primary_theme: Neural network-based power prediction for mobile CPUs
